yes: The post meets the category the question names, as the Gab Hate Corpus coding manual defines it. Assault on human dignity: it degrades a group, or a person because of their group, by asserting or implying inferiority, comparing them to animals or subhumans, using slurs meant to wound, spreading hateful stereotypes, or supporting hateful ideology such as white supremacy. Call for violence: it advocates or endorses violence, genocide, expulsion, exclusion or segregation against a group, or a person because of their group. Vulgar or offensive language: it uses vulgar, derogatory or abusive wording or personal insults, whether or not the post is hateful.
no: The post does not meet the category the question names under the coding manual. Insults or threats aimed at a person without invoking their group are neither an assault on dignity nor a call for violence; degrading a group without advocating aggression, expulsion or exclusion is not a call for violence; hateful or political views stated without vulgar, profane or abusive wording are not vulgar language; criticism of policies, parties or ideas that does not degrade people is none of these.
race or ethnicity: The hateful rhetoric mainly targets people for their race or ethnicity, for example anti-Black, anti-Asian, anti-Latino, anti-Arab or antisemitic attacks on Jews as a people (the manual codes antisemitism here).
nationality or region: The hateful rhetoric mainly targets people for their nationality, country or region of origin, including general xenophobia, attacks on immigrants as foreigners, or on named countries or regions.
gender: The hateful rhetoric mainly targets people for their gender or gender identity, for example anti-woman, anti-man or anti-trans attacks.
religion: The hateful rhetoric mainly targets people for their religion or spiritual beliefs, for example anti-Muslim or anti-Christian attacks on believers or the faith.
sexual orientation: The hateful rhetoric mainly targets people for their sexual orientation, for example gay, lesbian or bisexual people.
ideology: The hateful rhetoric mainly targets people for their ideology or worldview, such as liberals, leftists, conservatives or the right wing as a camp of believers, not as members of a party.
political affiliation: The hateful rhetoric mainly targets people for membership of a political organisation or party, such as Democrats or Republicans, or a named party's members or politicians.
health or disability: The hateful rhetoric mainly targets people for their mental or physical health status, mental illness or a physical disability.
